lines.trans: I will just set down two fixed cameras and head out.
Since I cannot sleep well outdoors either, I prepared a few things.
If you listen to at least some music, you should fall asleep more easily.
And try reading this—it is a book I always read right before bed.
Are you telling me to read a book right here right now?

lines.trans: It puts you right to sleep, and wear this cap tomorrow morning if your hair gets greasy.

I am not an outcast—it is not like I have no friends, I do have them!
Everyone is just too busy, and if this airs, people are going to misunderstand and think I am an outcast.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 거치 카메라 두 대만 놓고 나갈게요.
examples.trans: I will just set down two fixed cameras and head out.
Here the word for 'mounted, fixed' is key.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'camera'

examples.trans: Please move the camera over here.
I bought a new camera.

meanings.note: Attributive form of 둘 used directly before counter nouns (두 개, 두 사람).

examples.trans: Please give me two apples.
Let's meet at two o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 거치 카메라 두 대만 놓고 나갈게요.
examples.trans: I will just set down two fixed cameras and head out.
Here the word for 'only units' is key.

놓다.gloss: to put, to place, to leave

meanings.en: to put, to place, to leave
meanings.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to indicate leaving something in a certain state.

examples.trans: Please place it on the desk.
I left the door open.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room
meanings.note: 나- ('out') + 가다 ('to go')

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: noun outside

examples.trans: It rains outside.
Fell out of favor.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 저도 밖에서는 잠을 잘 못 자서요, 이것저것 준비했거든요.
examples.trans: Since I cannot sleep well outdoors either, I prepared a few things.
Here the word for 'sleep' is key.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.
Did you sleep well last night?
The baby is sleeping right now.

related.gloss: to wake up; to get up

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 저도 밖에서는 잠을 잘 못 자서요, 이것저것 준비했거든요.
examples.trans: Since I cannot sleep well outdoors either, I prepared a few things.
Here the word for 'this and that' is key.

meanings.note: Transitive verb taking -을/를.

examples.trans: I prepared the presentation materials in advance.
The time spent preparing for a trip is also enjoyable.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 음악이라도 들으시면 잠이 잘 오실 거예요.
examples.trans: If you listen to at least some music, you should fall asleep more easily.
Here the word for 'even just music' is key.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Spoken contraction of bound noun 것; used in -(으)ㄴ/는 거예요 to ask or explain a situation.

examples.trans: Where are you going right now?
That is mine.
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 그리고 이거 읽어보세요, 제가 자기 전에 꼭 읽는 책인데.
examples.trans: And try reading this—it is a book I always read right before bed.
This expression comes from 'try reading'.

examples.text: 나 마음 바뀌기 전에 빨리 계약서 보내는 게 좋을 거예요.
examples.trans: You had better send the contract quickly before I change my mind.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?

meanings.note: Emphasizes necessity or strong intention.
Used with holding or closing actions.

examples.trans: Definitely contact me tomorrow.
Please close the door tightly.
I want to read right now.
How about trying to read together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Counted with the counter 권.

examples.text: 서점에서 새 책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.trans: I bought a new book at the bookstore.
This book is good for beginners to read.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.
Did you hear about this tomorrow?
I was busy today because of tomorrow.

meanings.note: Short for 아침밥

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.
Did you eat breakfast?
Did you hear about this head, brain?
I was busy today because of head, brain.

떡지다.gloss: if it gets clumped and greasy

meanings.en: if it gets clumped and greasy
meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 잠이 잘 옵니다, 그리고 이거는 내일 아침에 머리 떡지면 쓰세요.
examples.trans: It puts you right to sleep, and wear this cap tomorrow morning if your hair gets greasy.
This expression comes from 'if it gets clumped and greasy'.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.

meanings.en: to talk on the phone, to have a phone conversation
meanings.note: More specific than 전화하다 ('to place a call'); focuses on having the conversation.

examples.trans: Can we talk on the phone for a moment?
I spoke with my mom on the phone this morning.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun referring to something near the listener or already mentioned. Routinely spoken as 그거. RR: geugeot; spoken geugeo.

examples.trans: That is my mobile phone.
That is really important.
Let's must edit together today.
I worked hard to must edit yesterday too.

meanings.note: Used for giving things to someone of equal or lower status.

examples.trans: I gave a gift.
Please give me some water.
Did you hear about this editing?
I was busy today because of editing.
It really is is loud, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is is loud, so and nice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 편집은 큰 사안이라서 제 소관은 아닙니다만.
examples.trans: Editing is a major matter, so it is not really within my authority, though.
Here the word for 'because it is an issue' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 편집은 큰 사안이라서 제 소관은 아닙니다만.
examples.trans: Editing is a major matter, so it is not really within my authority, though.
Here the word for 'jurisdiction, authority' is key.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 나 왕따 아니에요, 친구도 없는 거 아니야, 있어요!
examples.trans: I am not an outcast—it is not like I have no friends, I do have them!
Here the word for 'outcast, loner' is key.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Formed from 다 (all) + plural suffix -들

examples.trans: Has everyone been doing well?
Everyone, gather over here.

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem adjective: 바쁘다 + -아요 becomes 바빠요.

examples.trans: Work at the company is so busy these days.
If you're busy, please contact me later.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

meanings.note: Can refer to a single person or people/a crowd in general without a plural suffix.

examples.trans: There are many people in the cafeteria.
He is a good person.

examples.text: 오해할 수 있는 상황인 거 내가 충분히 알아.
examples.trans: I fully understand that this is a situation you could misunderstand.

examples.text: 두 분은 순수한 친구 사이신데 오해해서 상처받으면 어쩌나 해서요.
examples.trans: Since you two are pure friends, I worried she might misunderstand and get hurt.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
